I bought this game last time Steam had it for $5. I've been playing 20 days and after 3 days of the 30 day trial, I purchased my first month for after my trial ended, which bumped my trial to a paid membership. Just a couple days ago I took advantage of the Power of 2 offer from CCP where you can add a second paid account for $49.95 for 6 months, that's half price. I added 2 additional accounts so I'm playing 3 characters at the same time. When you join Eve as a paid member you'll receive the 2 holiday gift sets which have already been given to players plus the final one which comes out Dec 28. These items can be sold for millions in ISK in game.

Some of the people on here are trying to get you to use their friend referrals so they'll get free stuff from CCP. I'm not saying it's a bad thing, but it's bad form to advertise it on Steam. Do that sh__ somewhere else. Quit trying to rack up billions of dollars and free gifts by recruiting Eve players here.

After a month or so of dedicated playing, you'll be able to purchase PLEX in game with ISK (in game currency) that you earn, it costs around 550M (or so) ISK. You can also buy PLEX with a credit card for $20 and sell it in game for ISK to use to buy stuff in Eve. Essentially with dedication this game will pay for itself, by allowing you to buy PLEX in game and use that PLEX to pay for your subscription.

Eve looks a little intimidating at first, however the career tutorials help a lot. You'll be on your own in no time. There's also the Rookie Help chat room which you're logged into automatically for the first 30 days. Here you can ask any questions and friendly, helpful people like myself and tons of others will help you.

Lots of people will tell you to join a corp, I haven't yet and after 20 days I'm still having a blast playing alone. Corps are like guilds, you can mine together, run missions, have backup and protection in lawless areas, and get lower tax rates on commerce, in addition to a dedicated group of people to chat with. There are tons of corps out there with various interests like industry, piracy, bounty hunting, etc.

Join one if you want, but it's not necessary. There are also tons of chat rooms where you can get assistance on missions without joining a corp. The options in Eve are overwhelming, you can trade, mine, manufacture, research, find sites to scan for relics and hack into systems to retrieve valuable data. Don't think that EVE is all about PvP, it can be if you want. Sure there are some rough areas where other players will attack and destroy your ship, but that's where corps or friends come in. You can also avoid those areas if you want and stay in less dangerous systems.

Here are a few things which may answer some questions:

-you can't manually fly your ship, you select an object in space such as an asteroid belt, planet, complex, etc and warp to it. You can turn on your engine and fly slowly around if you want, but there are no barrel rolls, loops, or any of that stuff you see in sci-fi movies.

-you will have to work to get money, mining is the easiest option and people who've been playing for years still mine. It can and does get repetitive, aside from the occasional pirates, you basically just watch lasers and drones (if you're trained) do the work and you fly it back to a dock and sell it. I've seen people mention that they knit, watch TV, multitask, or other things to pass time. Personally I enjoy reading :P

-To attack you target a ship and click your weapon button. You can't fly around and manually aim.

-Training DOES TAKE TIME! Unlike other MMOs, shooting enemies and completing tasks doesn't earn you XP. Training is in real time and continues after you log off. Getting to the first level of basic skills takes only 7-10 minutes, second level on basic skills takes about 17-30 minutes, and 3rd level can take 1-3 hours, 4th 17 hours to a day, and 5th level takes a couple days AT LEAST! Advanced skills can take WEEKS of real time to train. You'll have to be patient, you can't start the game and go right into pirating or bounty hunting. When you start out your weapons will be weak, inaccurate, and have shorter range, you'll be limited to the ships you can pilot, you won't be able to add upgrades to your ship until you train for them first.

Hope this helps answer some questions and pique some interest in the game. This isn't a casual economic game. The economy is real and driven by players. Everything available for sale has been built by a player and those players manufacture with ore mined by other players. There is something for almost everyone in this game. You are a piece of a working machine in the Eve universe.

My char is 8 years old in eve. Get this game if you like:

- Grief. The game is designed to allow grief. People with secondary accounts will trick you into following them and make you lose your 1 billlion dollar ship in 0.5 seconds. Oh yeah fun.
- Singleplayer: I've never met less players or groups in a game which holds 50000 players at night. People really can't be bothered to group in EVE. It's so lonely in the void of space...
- Lonelyness: You can see your charcter run around in the space station but you can't see anyone else, W..T...F is this about. Hope they changed this since last time I checked.
- Negociating jump gates: If you like parking a large vehicle or spaceships, this game is for you. You will negociate millions of jump gates, its almost a flight simulator build around jump gates.
Solar systems are ridiculously small. The quality of the whole game would be better if "rooms" were bigger and the universe would hold less jumpgates.
- Months and Months of training: Ok you can train offline, prepare to be offline for months, good skills take 6 weeks to train. Good luck soldier.
- No high-end gameplay: Ok there is some higher level content, but you won't reach it by playing the game more. Things like lvl 5 missions or Wormholes are out of reach for most guilds, nevermind the individual player. Maybe if you pick your training well and find the right people, you might reach this after 1 year of EVE. Only the most hardcore players can do this.

Don't be fooled by the fleet combat video's. Guilds (corporations) who are big enough to take part in those fleet combat fights won't accept you unless you have months of xp. And even then only the best corporations are active in those, chances are you will never get to see it. Those video's are totally fake.

5€ to start EVE is a good deal. Now you only need 15€ x 11 to fund the rest of the year to get into the real deal with EVE.

If you're in low sec or 0.0 space and somebody kills you, CONCORD (in game NPC police) won't be able to help you. If you're in .5 or higher space CONCORD will kill the other player. There's no way for anyone to escape CONCORD. You go into low-security or null space with a couple of people or yes, you will get destroyed. Not everybody is a liar or a pirate in this game. Players can set bounties so if you click on a profile and their bounty is 2M ISK you can tell this person pissed off some people and it's best not to necessarily trust them right away.

Once you finish the download, go to eveonline.com and register a new account. If you don't get a screen that says the account has been created SOMETHING IS WRONG! I thought my account was created but if you submit and you get a blank sign up form again, that means something went wrong, probably with your password. Last time I checked the account creation page doesn't warn you if there's an error, it just resets. When you add time to your account use the CD key in Steam

I never said it was safe but I've never seen anybody attacked in high sec. I've left my computer for a few hours with a ship hovering in high sec and came back to find it intact. Eve can be dangerous, however don't make it sound as if piracy happens everywhere. People get the impression they'll be destroyed when they leave the dock, which isn't true. No need to scare off potential players.
